raw_response:
I farm the same 5 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I do not split the land between the two crops. I use the full 5 mu for winter wheat first, then after harvest I plant summer maize on the same ground. I have done this for many years, so I start from what worked before and only adjust a little. With well irrigation, I will not be too stingy on water, because in our place one missed watering can cost more grain than the electricity bill costs me. My schooling is not high, but after farming 30 years I do look at the field more carefully now. Wheat needs a stronger base and steady water, especially for tillering and grain filling. Maize grows fast after the rainy season starts, but if fertilizer is short it will show immediately, so I will keep enough nitrogen on it. On 5 mu I still count costs closely, but I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. I also watch what nearby farmers do, and around here improved wheat seed and hybrid maize are already normal, so I will follow that. For wheat I will rotary till after maize, put more base fertilizer, irrigate about 3 times, and spray 2 times if needed for weeds and disease. For maize I will usually rotary till or lightly prepare the land after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed, give enough nitrogen, irrigate about 2 times with my well if rain is not enough, and spray 2 times for weeds and insects. That is the safer way for my family this year.
